# 好多鱼图文

Private self-media account matrix. Humans sign in with username/password. Authorized AI integrations use scoped Bearer credentials issued by the administrator.

Public documentation: /api-docs
OpenAPI: /openapi.json
API base: /api/v1

Only successfully published articles are recorded. Cumulative observations and daily period metrics are separate. Read the OpenAPI schema, use Idempotency-Key for writes, and verify saved records by ID. Never invent missing metrics. Do not request an administrator password for API access.

Atomic daily snapshot exception: GET /api/v1/snapshot?date=YYYY-MM-DD accepts exactly one explicit valid date; GET /api/v1/snapshot/index accepts no query parameters. Both are read-only current projections and never write business data or Notion. They require the existing matrix_session of the explicitly configured PUBLIC_BUSINESS_USER_ID, or anonymous public access only when PUBLIC_BUSINESS_MODE=1. PUBLIC_BUSINESS_USER_ID and DAILY_NOTES_OWNER_ID must be explicitly configured even in private mode. Owner sessions retain all-account visibility; anonymous scope follows existing configured accounts plus public-created accounts minus public-deleted accounts. Any Authorization header is rejected with 403, including Bearer/API keys; other logged-in users receive 403. No new API-key permission is provided.

Snapshot success is wrapped in data, with snapshot_format, projection=current, date, scope_id, timezone=Asia/Shanghai, generated_at, content_hash, and a nested data object containing todos, templates, notes, accounts, articles, observations, daily_metrics, habit30days. Notes use the existing public daily-note owner, exclude soft-deleted records, and contain no memo. Articles include run-date drafts, publication-day and observation/metric-linked records, preserving lifecycle, nulls and decoded pipeline JSON. habit30days covers D-29 through D, counts distinct completed days per current active template, and uses threshold 21. Empty dates still return current account/template frames and the habit window.

The index returns complete=true, scope_id, every real business date in ascending order with its daily content_hash, and index_hash. There is no recent-days cutoff or partial-success truncation. Hashes exclude generated_at, include scope, canonicalize object keys and entity collections, and preserve nested business-array order. This is not a historical database backup. Compare the union of current indexed dates and previously saved dates; reread changed and disappeared dates to detect old edits, final-record deletion and date moves. A changed scope_id requires rebaselining, never deletion inference. Each request is atomic including authorization, but index and daily reads can race: on a daily hash mismatch, reread the index and affected detail, and recheck the index before applying the batch.

Whole-request limits: 45 SQL calls including authorization/revision checks/retries, 4000 projected rows, 1MiB source projection JSON, 1000 indexed dates, 8MiB total hash input, 1MiB response, 100000 observed rows_read, and 50 accounts. Limits return 413 SNAPSHOT_LIMIT, never partial data; unavailable rows_read receipts return 503 SNAPSHOT_BUDGET. rows_read is observed after queries and is not a hard pre-query scan or CPU cap; edge CPU behavior remains unverified. Successful responses use Cache-Control: private, no-store and Vary: Cookie, Authorization.

Life/work notes: category defaults to life for legacy compatibility; category=work is independent. Snapshot v1 is unchanged; notes=all explicitly selects complete dual-category v2 and work-only dates. Backups are v8, retaining v1-v7 isolated empty-target restore compatibility.

Workbench additions: /note-entries supports multiple stable UUID life/work records per day (complete live list <=200/category/day), paged distinct dates, item reads, CAS PUT, explicit delete/restore, and editor-only metadata receipts. Stored server timestamps are preserved; legacy /daily-notes remains independent. /work-reminders?date returns items (<=100 live/day); PUT uses immutable date/source_key and <=16KiB summary; update the existing UUID for a repeated day/source. Both modules retain DAILY_NOTES_OWNER_ID session/public same-origin editing, save_id receipts and shared notes rate limits; Bearer provides no write capability. No new cron or external notification is configured.

GET /workbench-snapshot?date and /workbench-snapshot/index are a separate read-only format, haoduoyu-workbench-snapshot-v1. Existing snapshot v1/v2 stay unchanged. Both return a complete identical all-date entity/tombstone manifest plus undated memos, stable scope-qualified IDs, source timestamps, per-entity hashes, manifest_hash/global_content_hash; daily data contains todos, life_notes, work_notes, work_reminders, memo_groups, memos. Index date hashes match daily date_content_hash; daily content_hash also covers undated content. Deduplicate by scope_id/entity_id, preserve legacy/new identities, rebaseline changed scope, and recheck manifests before applying cross-request sync. Uses existing snapshot owner-session/public policy, rejects every Authorization header, additionally requires explicit MEMOS_OWNER_ID, reads every source completely, and shares the documented 45-SQL/4000-row/1MiB-source/1000-date/8MiB-hash/1MiB-response/100000-observed-rows_read/50-account bounds; 413/503 errors never mean partial success.

/account-profiles reads only authorized account mappings (<=1000, otherwise422). Optional profile_url on account creation/update is locally canonicalized for known Toutiao, Zhihu and WeChat public homepages; it never logs into or fetches platforms. Visible canonical duplicates return200/profile_reused:true; out-of-scope duplicates reveal no record. GET /backup now exports v9 with note_entries, work_reminders and account_profiles; v1-v8 restore remains operator-only, explicit and empty-target-only. No HTTP restore, platform tokens, Tencent integration or Notion automation change is introduced.

AI reports: OpenAPI describes GET /api/v1/ai-reports?offset=0, PUT /api/v1/ai-reports/{uuid}, and DELETE /api/v1/ai-reports/{uuid}. In PUBLIC_BUSINESS_MODE=1, anyone can read and write without identity authentication; author is self-reported, not verified. Public PUT requires Origin exactly equal to the site origin, X-Public-Business: 1, and application/json. Supply exactly author and content; conventionally start content with the work date YYYY-MM-DD on its first line (the server does not enforce the date). Generate a lowercase UUID once and retry the same normalized body with that UUID: 201 creates, 200 replays, and 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT signals different content. Lists return at most 100 items and has_more; increase offset by 100 to continue. Each item has content_hash, a lowercase SHA-256 digest of stable JSON over id, author, content and created_at. The user has approved deletion of any single report by any visitor in public mode. Deletion is permanent and cannot be recovered; author signatures are self-reported and unauthenticated. To delete, send DELETE with application/json {"expected_hash":"<content_hash from GET>","save_id":"<lowercase UUID for this operation>"}, same-origin Origin and X-Public-Business: 1. A stale expected_hash returns 409 VERSION_CONFLICT; reread the list before deciding whether to retry. The same identity repeating the identical request with the same save_id replays success, unless a record with that ID exists again (409); using that save_id for a different request returns 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. A missing report returns 404. After deletion, PUT with the same report UUID returns 409 AI_REPORT_DELETED to prevent resurrection by a delayed create retry. Author is 1–120 Unicode code points; content is at most 16 KiB UTF-8 after normalization and trimming; the JSON body is at most 256 KiB. Public writes, including rejected bodies and retries, are limited per owner and module per process to 60/minute and 2000/UTC day; this is not a global limit. Errors include 400 validation/JSON, 401/403 access, 404 invalid route/UUID, 413 body too large, 415 content type, 429 AI_REPORTS_RATE_LIMIT, 500 internal error, and 503 configuration unavailable. Error responses contain error.code, error.message and request_id. Explicit invalid credentials do not fall back to anonymous access. An owner session also works with Origin and CSRF on writes; Bearer keys do not grant access.

Content review: independent namespace /api/v1/review; phase-one UI ?page=review&account=V字 displays V字/Toutiao. Account defaults to V字 (API accepts other valid account strings); platform is only toutiao. Old article/observation/daily-metric APIs and existing backend data remain independent, with no automatic migration. The page reads data; write via API, with no page edit forms. Business reports, metrics and playbook content are for Grok BOT to supply; documentation examples are not seeded data.

All 21 review operations: for each of articles, snapshots, reports, playbooks, GET /api/v1/review/{resource}, GET /api/v1/review/{resource}/{uuid}, PUT /api/v1/review/{resource}/{uuid}, PATCH /api/v1/review/{resource}/{uuid}, DELETE /api/v1/review/{resource}/{uuid}; plus PUT /api/v1/review/snapshots:batch. In PUBLIC_BUSINESS_MODE=1 every visitor may read, create, update and permanently delete all four public resource types without identity authentication. Signatures and source_chat are self-reported, not verified. Public writes require exact same-origin Origin, X-Public-Business: 1 and application/json; owner-session writes require Origin and X-CSRF-Token. Explicit invalid credentials never fall back to anonymous access; Bearer does not grant access. This exception grants no permission over passwords, keys, backup or other APIs. JSON requests are capped at256KiB. Public attempts including rejected payloads and retries use a separate review per-owner per-process limit60/minute and2000/UTC day, not a global limit.

Review lists return data:{items,has_more,read_revision}, at most100 rows; offset defaults0 and increases by100 while has_more, maximum9007199254740991, no leading zeros. Pass the first nonnegative safe-integer read_revision on subsequent pages;409 READ_REVISION_CHANGED means restart at offset0. It detects cross-page changes, not a historical snapshot. All returned items and details include content_hash. Article filters:account/from/to, ordered published_at DESC,created_at DESC,id DESC. Snapshot filters:account,article_id (combined; account matches the related review article), ordered snapshot_date DESC,id DESC. Report filters:account/period_type/from/to, ordered period_start DESC,created_at DESC,id DESC. Playbook filter:account, ordered version DESC,created_at DESC,id DESC. Dates are inclusive; article from/to filters run before pagination using the Asia/Shanghai date of published_at, while report dates use the unchanged period_start calendar date. Article grouping, daily statistics, library date filters, trend-day assignment and timestamp displays use Asia/Shanghai (Beijing time), independent of the client timezone. Unknown or repeated queries are rejected.

Review fields: articles require title (<=2000UTF-8 bytes), account defaults V字, platform defaults toutiao; platform_article_id(<=240),url/published_at,topic_category(<=240),title_pattern(<=1000),sample_title(<=2000),sample_url,image_count,source_chat(<=4096) default null. URLs are credential-free HTTP(S), <=4096bytes; published_at is a strict YYYY-MM-DD date or timezone-bearing ISO timestamp. When an exact time is known, BOT should submit it with +08:00, for example 2026-10-27T04:05:00+08:00; the server normalizes timestamp storage to UTC (2026-10-26T20:05:00.000Z in this example), and its Beijing day is 2026-10-27. Date-only values remain unchanged; do not invent midnight for a date-only source, and use null for unknown times. snapshot_date, period_start, period_end and published_on are calendar dates and are never shifted by eight hours. articles also return created_at/updated_at. snapshots require article_id(new review UUID) and snapshot_date; impressions,fan_impressions,reads,fan_reads,likes,comments,reposts,shares,favorites are nullable nonnegative safe integers; ctr/completion_rate are nullable percentages0–100, avg_read_seconds/revenue nullable nonnegative numbers. traffic_sources/audience are nullable objects, completion_curve nullable object or array. All snapshot optional fields default null; snapshots have no created_at/updated_at. reports require period_type(daily|three_day|weekly),period_start,period_end(start<=end); account defaults V字, verdicts defaults{}, findings defaults{verified:[],overturned:[]}, summary_md defaults empty, metrics defaults{}, playbook_version defaults null or positive safe integer. verdicts maps article UUID to exactly{verdict:爆|中|扑,reason:nonempty <=8192bytes}; findings has exactly verified/overturned arrays of objects with rule_id(<=120bytes), allowing evidence JSON. playbooks require positive version and published_on; account defaults V字, content_md/changelog_md empty, rules[], sent_to_gemini_at null(date or ISO timestamp). Each rule is exactly{rule_id,section,text}; rule_id<=120bytes unique within rules, text<=16KiB, section=keep_topic|drop_topic|title|body|audience|checklist. sent_to_gemini_at only records a supplied time and sends nothing; exact times should also include +08:00 on input, are stored as UTC, and display in Asia/Shanghai, while date-only values remain unchanged. reports/playbooks also return created_at. All resources return id/content_hash; server created_at/updated_at and content_hash are read-only.

Review inputs reject unknown top-level fields. Text normalizes line endings and trims; single-line fields forbid newline/tab, all reject malformed Unicode/control characters. Account <=120UTF-8 bytes. Unknown metrics stay null, actual zero stays0, no metric is invented. JSON fields are direct object/array values, <=64KiB each, <=12deep and10000value nodes, no __proto__/prototype/constructor keys or nonfinite numbers. Markdown may be empty; otherwise <=128KiB. PUT uses a lowercase UUID stable across retries:201new,200same normalized full content including defaults,409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT for different content. Unique business keys:articles(account,nonnull platform_article_id), snapshots(article_id,snapshot_date), reports(account,period_type,period_start), playbooks(account,version). Conflict409 REVIEW_UNIQUE_CONFLICT includes error.existing_id; GET that ID before deciding. PATCH needs current expected_hash and at least one writable field; omitted fields stay, JSON fields replace wholesale, nullable fields clear with null. Stale hash409 VERSION_CONFLICT; reread and resolve, never blindly overwrite. Unknown PATCH outcome requires GET reconciliation.

Review DELETE is permanent and cannot be recovered; every visitor may delete in public mode. Send exactly{expected_hash:<current GET content_hash>,save_id:<operation lowercase UUID>}; articles alone also accepts cascade_snapshots:true, required when snapshots exist (otherwise409 ARTICLE_HAS_SNAPSHOTS). Same identity with identical save_id/path/body replays200; different use409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT; stale hash409 VERSION_CONFLICT; missing record404. Persistent tombstones reject old PUT with409 REVIEW_DELETED and prevent resurrection, including cascaded snapshots. No restore endpoint. Snapshot batch body is exactly{items:[{id,...snapshot create fields}]},1–200items, ordered independent per-item data.items:{id,status,data?|error?}; HTTP200 is not all-success, inspect each status. New201/same200/conflict409; failed items do not roll back successes. Keep every item UUID/content on retries.

Review errors use{error:{code,message,existing_id?},request_id}; statuses400(validation/JSON),401/403(access/CSRF),404(NOT_FOUND|ARTICLE_NOT_FOUND),409(IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT,VERSION_CONFLICT,READ_REVISION_CHANGED,REVIEW_UNIQUE_CONFLICT,REVIEW_DELETED,ARTICLE_HAS_SNAPSHOTS),413(BODY_TOO_LARGE),415(CONTENT_TYPE),429(REVIEW_RATE_LIMIT),500(INTERNAL_ERROR),503(NOTES_CONFIG|REVIEW_CONFIG). Read OpenAPI for all exact request/response schemas. Never execute documentation examples or seed fabricated business conclusions.

Review clarification: each HTTP public-write request counts once, including a batch of up to200; duplicate batch IDs are allowed and processed in order. Unknown storage/network failure can return an overall500 after prior items committed: GET each original UUID and retry with the original UUID/body. Batch item failures return input string id or null and code/message/optional extra fields, without per-item request_id; use the overall X-Request-Id. Article DELETE data additionally includes deleted_snapshots; ARTICLE_HAS_SNAPSHOTS error additionally includes snapshot_count. Snapshot account filtering joins the related owner-scoped review article and can combine with article_id.
